$comment: Settings for the local release-video pipeline. Everything here is a
knob a human turns; nothing an AI model is allowed to write.
Run `npm run doctor` after changing anything in `tools` or `voice`.
Paths are relative to the REPOSITORY root, not to release-video, because
these assets belong to the product rather than to this tool.
Used to build the opening logo card and the closing download card.
Both are rendered as HTML through the same headless browser that takes
the screenshots, so layout and fonts behave the way they would on a page.

tools.$comment: Absolute paths or bare names resolved on PATH.

$comment: NVENC presets run p1 (fastest) to p7 (best quality). p6 is the
sweet spot for screen content. Set `encoder` to libx264 to render
without a GPU — everything else stays identical.
Ken Burns defaults. A scene whose feature declares a DOM anchor gets
its focus point measured from that element's real bounding box, so
the zoom lands on the thing being talked about rather than the
middle of the screenshot.
engine: mistral | voicebox | sapi | command | silence
voicebox — local Voicebox REST server (your cloned voice). Start it
first; the pipeline only ever talks to it over HTTP, so
TTS never shares VRAM with ffmpeg or whisper.
sapi     — Windows built-in speech. Zero install, generic voice.
Use it to get a watchable first cut today.
command  — any CLI that writes a WAV. See `command` below.
silence  — no audio; durations estimated from word count. For
checking timing and motion without generating speech.
referenceWav/referenceText are the consented clone source. Record
10-20s of clean speech and put the exact transcript beside it.
See assets/voice/README.md.
Mistral's hosted TTS with a cloned voice.
UNLIKE EVERY OTHER ENGINE HERE, THIS IS NOT LOCAL. Narration text
leaves the machine and the service is billed per request. The
narration cache therefore matters more, not less: an unchanged
scene is never re-sent.
The API key is read from the environment variable named by
apiKeyEnv and is never stored in this file, which is committed.
voiceId comes from the voice you cloned in Mistral's console.

sapi.$comment: Run `npm run video -- voices` to list installed SAPI voices.

$comment: argv template for an arbitrary TTS CLI. {{text}}, {{out}},
{{referenceWav}} and {{referenceText}} are substituted as single
argv entries — never through a shell, so narration text is never
parsed as a command. A command containing a path separator is
resolved relative to this project.
Configured for Piper: neural, CPU-only, so it never competes with
NVENC for the 6 GB of VRAM. Voices live in assets/voice/piper and
are fetched with:
.venv-tts/Scripts/python -m piper.download_voices \
--download-dir assets/voice/piper en_GB-alan-medium
Swap -m for en_US-ryan-high for a slower, higher-quality US voice.
This is the shipped default because it is local, free and needs no
key. To clone a real voice, either set engine to "mistral" (hosted,
billed, fast) or point argv at scripts/chatterbox-speak.py (local,
free, minutes per paragraph on CPU). See README.md.
--length-scale is pace: 1.0 is the model's own, lower is faster.
0.88 reads at about the speed of a presenter who knows the
material. Below ~0.8 it starts to clip its own consonants.
--sentence-silence is the gap between sentences, in seconds.
Both change the narration cache key, so editing either one
regenerates every line on the next `build --from voice`.
Optional narration polish. The pipeline produces a complete,
deterministic script from the release catalog with `enabled: false`;
the model only ever rewrites prose, never timings, paths or
coordinates, and its output is schema-validated and length-capped
before it is used.
provider: ollama | openai-compatible (LM Studio, llama.cpp server)
Word-level timings come from faster-whisper if `align` is true and
the CLI is on PATH; otherwise captions are one cue per scene, timed
from the measured WAV duration (still correct, just less granular).
